paper.title_en: High-power Powder Bed Fusion–Laser Based of Dragon Copper: Microstructure, mechanical properties, and application to next-generation gravitational wave detectors
paper.abstract_en: The additive manufacturing of pure copper, via Powder Bed Fusion-Laser Based (PBF-LB), is intrinsically challenging due to the high thermal conductivity and low absorptivity of copper in the near-infrared range. As a result, low powered PBF-LB systems fail to produce fully dense copper parts, introducing porosity and microstructural defects. To address these limitations, the incorporation of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into copper powders has recently led to the development of a novel nanocomposite material, known as Dragon Copper. This innovative material has demonstrated in a previous work that even a very low CNTs content (0.1 wt%) is sufficient to significantly reduce near-infrared reflectivity of copper, thereby enabling stable PBF-LB processing at low laser power (∼175 W). However, it remains unclear whether the benefits of CNTs addition persist when using high-powered PBF-LB systems, where pure copper processing is already partially improved. In this work, Dragon Copper is processed using a 1 kW PBF-LB system to assess its performance under industrially relevant conditions. The results show that Dragon Copper achieves near-full densification and exhibits an approximately 20% increase in ultimate tensile strength compared to pure copper, while preserving high electrical and thermal conductivities. These findings support the scalability of Dragon Copper processing for industrial applications requiring structural integrity combined with electrical and thermal performance. Finally, the mechanical behaviour of PBF-LB-manufactured Dragon Copper flexural joints is investigated from 9 K to room temperature, demonstrating its suitability for cryogenic applications and ultra-low-noise components for next-generation gravitational wave detectors like the forthcoming Einstein Telescope.
